library_preparation_preflight.summary: langchain4j-http-client is only the HttpClient SPI (HttpClient, HttpClientBuilder, HttpRequest, SuccessfulHttpResponse, ServerSentEvent parsers and listeners). It needs no extra dependency or Docker image. Tests can use an in-process JDK HttpServer, so I'm adding guidance only.
library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: Do not add Docker images or extra Maven dependencies. The generated scaffold already pulls in the library and its transitive langchain4j-core. Exercise the module's own API: build HttpRequest objects (method, url, headers, body, form data) and run SuccessfulHttpResponse and ServerSentEvent parsing, including DefaultServerSentEventParser, ServerSentEventContext and the listener callbacks. Drive these with in-memory data or a local `com.sun.net.httpserver.HttpServer` bound to 127.0.0.1 on an ephemeral port. Do not depend on a real HttpClient implementation (langchain4j-http-client-jdk or -okhttp), because this artifact ships none. If a test needs a client, write a small HttpClient implementation inside the test, or call `HttpClientBuilderLoader` only if an implementation is on the classpath. The loader uses ServiceLoader, so only add a `META-INF/services` entry for a test-local builder if the test deliberately exercises that path. No environment variables or system properties are required.
risks: If a test calls HttpClientBuilderLoader with no implementation on the classpath, it throws a 'no HTTP client implementation found' error. Provide a test-local SPI implementation or avoid that call.
ServiceLoader-based discovery may need extra reachability metadata, which local native-image verification should reveal.
